title: Clock-skew-aware log reassembler with sealed windowing for cross-region correlation
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Problem: Cross-region traces and multi-cluster services produce log events with inconsistent clocks and partial ordering. Downstream Loki/ELK consumers and correlation tools rely on stable ordering for span-log joins and alerting thresholds, but current ingest pipelines credit the producer timestamp and then fall back to arrival order, leading to noisy latency/error dashboards and missed correlations.

Proposal: Implement a clock-skew-aware reassembly stage in the ingest pipeline that uses sealed-windowing + watermark heuristics to produce a deterministic, best-effort ordering per correlation key (trace_id or session_id). Key components: 1) Windowing: group events by tenant + correlation key into sealed time-windows (configurable size per workload). 2) Watermarks: compute an event-time watermark per shard using hybrid heuristics (producer timestamp distribution, cross-region RTT estimates, and cluster monotonic counters). 3) Deterministic tie-breaker: within sealed windows, order events by (event_time, producer_offset, partition_sequence, sha1(payload_prefix)) to preserve determinism across retries. 4) Skew reconciliation: apply clock-skew-adjustments when obvious backwards jumps occur (e.g., >5s across same trace) and annotate events with original_timestamp and reconciled_timestamp. 5) Backpressure & memory controls: implement size/time eviction policy, per-tenant soft-limits, and an admission path that tags large out-of-order spikes for fast-path ejection to preserve SLOs. 6) Observability: emit metrics for watermark lag, reorder-rate, events-reconciled, and eviction_count; expose debug traces for problematic traces to the Console.

Why this approach: Sealed windows allow bounded waiting to repair out-of-order arrivals while keeping latency predictable. Watermarks adapt to workload characteristics and cross-region latencies, minimizing unnecessary holding. Deterministic tie-breakers make downstream replays/compactions reproducible for SLO-sensitive dashboards.

Non-goals: this ticket does not implement long-term storage reordering in cold tier or change model selection logic in the serving runtime. It focuses on the ingest reassembler component and its contract with the downstream log fanout service.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Ingest reassembler implemented and deployed behind feature flag in staging.
2) For synthetic cross-region test, reorder-rate reduced by >= 75% and trace-log join success increased by >= 30% versus baseline.
3) Metrics: watermark_lag_p95 < configured window_size; eviction_count within 5% of expected under controlled spike.
4) All reconciled events include original_timestamp and reconciled_timestamp fields in the enriched payload.
5) Rollout playbook and rollback plan documented; Console dashboard with watermark lag and reorder-rate panels added.
6) No customer-facing error budget regression observed in canary for 48 hours at low traffic, 24 hours at high traffic.
